chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Zurara, from Al-Hasan Al-Bazzaz, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Shall I inform you of the most difficult of what Allah has imposed upon His creation? Three things.' I said, 'Yes.' He said: 'Fairness with the people from yourself, and equalizing your brother, and remembering Allah in every place.' He said: 'Indeed, I do not mean (merely saying) 'Glory be to Allah, and Praise be to Allah, and there is no god except Allah, and Allah is the Greatest', and even though this is from that, but (rather) remembering Allah, Majestic and Mighty, in every place, when you advance upon obedience or upon disobedience.'

key_terms.إِنْصَافُ النَّاسِ مِنْ نَفْسِكَ: Fairness with people from oneself (giving others what you give yourself)

ai.seo_question: What are the three most difficult obligations imposed by Allah according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights three profound obligations: selfless justice towards others, active solidarity with one's brother, and continuous divine remembrance (dhikr). He distinguishes this true dhikr from mere verbal recitation, defining it as a state of God-consciousness that persists whether one is engaged in obedience or, notably, in sin, reflecting the Shia emphasis on inner awareness over ritualistic formality.
